Observations: The first-layer weights are small and fairly uniformly distributed across all input rows, so there is no obvious localized spatial pattern for any single channel. The outer wall border is always present in channel 3, and its weights are spread across many hidden units, acting like a constant bias input. Channel 0 (agent), channel 1 (moving objects), and channel 2 (reward targets) all have similar small-magnitude weights, suggesting the network does not rely on a few highly localized cells for these channels. The output biases are  
`b3 = [-0.133, -0.132, 0.084, -0.172, -0.073]`,  
so action 2 (down) has the only positive bias, while no-op, up, left, and right are all slightly negative. In W3, some hidden units strongly favor down, e.g. row 13 has `0.168` for action 2, and row 25 has `0.172` for action 2, but these are not decisive on their own.

Reasoning: The observation channels map almost exactly onto Sokoban: channel 0 is the player, channel 1 is boxes (objects that move when pushed), channel 2 is target squares (reward targets), channel 3 is walls/obstacles, and channel 4 is the previous frame. Other grid games are less consistent: Pac-Man would typically have many reward pellets and autonomous ghosts, whereas here the “moving objects” channel does not show the kind of strong, localized weight structure one might expect for constantly moving enemies. Snake would have no separate moving objects. Frogger would have moving cars and a goal row, but its reward is usually a goal region rather than “reward targets.” The 10×10 grid with an outer wall border and an 8×8 playable interior is also characteristic of many Sokoban levels. The slight default preference for moving down is not enough to identify the game by itself, but it is compatible with a Sokoban agent whose starting position and level layout often require downward movement.

Game: Sokoban.

Description: The agent controls a player in a walled 10×10 grid and moves up, down, left, right, or no-op to push boxes onto designated target squares. Reward is given for placing boxes on targets, and the episode ends when all boxes are on targets.

Confidence: 78%
